title: Sta. Rita Ampalaya: Characteristics
metaDescription: Sta. Rita ampalaya is an IPB UPLB bred open pollinated ampalaya variety. See its days to harvest, yield, pest ratings, traits and where it grows best.
excerpt: Sta. Rita ampalaya is an IPB UPLB bred open pollinated ampalaya variety, also sold or known as Santa Rita ampalaya or Sta. Rita OPV. It is not a registered variety, so the facts here come from its seller and farm sources.

blocks.text: If you came here looking for Santa Rita ampalaya or Sta. Rita OPV, this is the same ampalaya. The facts below come from its seller and from farm sources, each one listed at the end. Compare it with the others in our [ampalaya variety finder](/crop-varieties/ampalaya), or see [every crop variety](/crop-varieties) we list. blocks.text: How long does it take, and how much does it yield?

Days to harvest, by the seller's count: first harvest about 50 days after transplanting (Allied sheet). Yield, by the seller's count: about 7.7 t/ha in a 2006 wet season trial in La Union, tied for the highest of five entries. No trial on record checks these figures yet, so treat them as the seller's own and compare with farms near you before you plan a season around it.

Once you know the day count, anee.io dates every task from each lot's own planting day, with [the growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside it.
Is it resistant to pests and diseases?
No pest or disease ratings are published for this variety. So treat it as untested, and scout every week.

The pests and diseases that hit ampalaya fields most often: [downy mildew of cucurbits](/diseases/downy-mildew), [melon fly](/pests/melon-fly), [squash beetle](/pests/squash-beetle), [anthracnose](/diseases/anthracnose), [Cercospora leaf spot](/diseases/cercospora-leaf-spot). Our [pest finder](/pests) and [disease finder](/diseases) help you name what you see.
What its seller and farm sources say

items: **Days to harvest:** First harvest about 50 days after transplanting (Allied sheet).
**Yield:** About 7.7 t/ha in a 2006 wet season trial in La Union, tied for the highest of five entries.
**Fruit:** Cylindrical, dark green, thick fleshed, about 33 to 35 cm long.

blocks.text: Why farmers know it: an IPB UPLB open pollinated ampalaya, one of the two top yielders in a 2006 DMMMSU wet season trial, and still packed by Allied Botanical (Condor). These are the seller's own figures, from its own trials. So plant a small area first, and compare it with your usual ampalaya on the same ground.
Where and when to plant Sta. Rita ampalaya

Pick by fruit: long and light green for most markets, short and dark for the bitter lovers. Hybrids yield more on a trellis, and some are bred to tolerate the downy mildew of the wet season. Before planting, get the field ready with our guide: [Pagtatanim ng gulay](/crops/pagtatanim-ng-gulay).

items: Buy sealed packs or tagged sacks from an accredited dealer, and check the packing date and germination rate.
Ask your municipal agriculturist or nearby farmers how it did in your area last season.
Try it on a small area first, beside the variety you usually plant, before you switch the whole farm.

items.q: Is Santa Rita ampalaya the same as Sta. Rita?
items.a: Yes. Santa Rita ampalaya is another name for Sta. Rita. Seed sellers use both, so ask for either one.
Yes. It is open pollinated, so seed from a clean, isolated field grows true. Still, certified seed gives the best start every few seasons.

items.q: Where can I buy seed of Sta. Rita?
items.a: Ask an accredited seed dealer in your province, the seller named on this page or your municipal agriculturist. Look for the certified seed tag or a sealed pack before you pay.
